title: The degree of a compositum over one factor is at most the degree of the other
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a field and $F\subseteq K$, $F\subseteq M$ subfields of $\Omega$ [def-pc-field-extension] such that $K/F$ is finite, of degree $[K:F]$ (the dimension of $K$ as an $F$-vector space). Let $KM\subseteq\Omega$ be the compositum, the smallest subfield of $\Omega$ containing $K$ and $M$. Then $KM/M$ is finite and $[KM:M]\le[K:F]$.

source.place: Algebra, used without statement in the proof of Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962: 'this construction leads to a new situation with [L : L_sep] < [K : K_sep]'); compositum as in Fields, Definition Tag 09ID (definition-compositum, line 3618) and the remark after it (KM is generated by K over M)

mathlib_searches.query: degree of compositum E(L) over E is at most degree of L over F

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take Lean's F := F, E := M, K := Ω (with the tower F → M → Ω) and L := K as an IntermediateField F Ω; the instance Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K is Algebra.IsAlgebraic.of_finite (Mathlib/RingTheory/Algebraic/Integral.lean:108) from K/F finite; IntermediateField.adjoin M K is the compositum KM, and Module.rank M (KM) ≤ Module.rank F K < ℵ₀ gives KM/M finite with finrank ≤ [K:F].
